properties.name: weakcrypto:config
properties.value: skill pq-crypto, 2 scouts, max iterations 400, build bbcd802706e4

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SSH control channels from the orchestrator/fleet/runner to rented GPU hosts (vast.ai) run with StrictHostKeyChecking=no and UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null — the tunnels authenticate nothing and are MITM-able. Changeable here: pin known_hosts per host instead.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The QSB bounty-search engine: recovers secp256k1 pubkeys from ECDSA signatures and grinds locktimes/subsets so the digest of the recovered pubkey parses as valid DER. ECDSA-secp256k1 is Shor-vulnerable, but on-chain signature verification is Bitcoin-consensus-bound — observable here, replaceable only by a soft fork (the repo's own paper/QSB.tex proposes exactly that migration). The local tooling (libsecp256k1 from apt, unpinned) is changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Opt-in "reproducible keygen": when a --seed is passed, the QSBScriptBuilder's secp256k1 key generation (bitcoin_tx.py generate_keys draws privkeys from os.urandom) becomes deterministic from a Mersenne Twister seed. Predictable keys if seed mode is ever used for real funds; the patch also affects every other os.urandom consumer while active. Changeable here: use a CSPRNG-backed derivation for reproducibility instead.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP39 mnemonic-to-seed derivation feeding BIP32 wallet key derivation for the QSB funding/spending transactions. 2048 is the BIP39-specified count, kept as the canonical PBKDF2 asset (the plain PBKDF2 object ALG-4de3b020 is the same asset). Changeable here only by leaving the BIP39 standard.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Key-material reference: the orchestrator's SSH client identity is an Ed25519 key (uploads/control to GPU rental hosts). SSH userauth signatures are Ed25519 — Shor-vulnerable. Changeable here by regenerating the key; note OpenSSH currently has no PQ userauth, so this is a classical dependency to migrate on OpenSSH's schedule.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test-only exercise of the project's own secp256k1 module's ECDSA (sign + recover), confirming the same code the production wallet-signing and hit-verification chains use. Quantum-unsafe; migration is ML-DSA-65.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The SHA-256 backbone of the Bitcoin-side pipeline (txids, sighashes, hash160 halves) plus SHA-256 integrity checks on the zips uploaded to GPU hosts. Not Shor-relevant (hashes only face Grover); rating A- appropriate. Changeable only where the Bitcoin protocol allows.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CUDA Keccak-f[1600] with ORIGINAL Keccak padding (0x01/0x80 — pre-FIPS-202), i.e. Keccak-256 truncated to a 160-bit digest of the (x,y) secp256k1 coordinates — Ethereum-style address derivation, computed on-GPU by the search kernels (GPUHash.h is compiled into qsb_search.cu/qsb_allgpu.cu per the Makefile). Quantum-safe beyond Grover's square-root; first-party code, changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP32 hierarchical wallet derivation for the QSB funding keys (master key from "Bitcoin seed", then private child derivation), mirrored in fund_qsb.py. HMAC-SHA512 is CNSA-2.0-grade; the keys it derives are secp256k1 and migrate with ML-DSA. Canonical HMAC asset (the SHA-384/512 object ALG-8c748911 is the same asset).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same BIP39 wallet-seed derivation asset as ALG-a861135a — kept as one entry so a reader references the low-iterations finding instead of chasing both.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: At all three sites SHA-512 exists only inside HMAC-SHA512 (BIP32 derivation); the MAC object is the accurate identity. SHA-512 is CNSA 2.0-grade; nothing to migrate at the hash layer.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CRITICAL companion finding: in qsb_pipeline.py the CSPRNG is monkeypatched to Mersenne Twister (os.urandom = lambda n: random.randbytes(n) / random.getrandbits) around QSBScriptBuilder.generate_keys() whenever --seed is passed, and always in cmd_test (random.seed(42)) — HORS puzzle secrets and pin/round keys generated in those modes are NOT CSPRNG-derived and are seed-recoverable (weak-PRNG side is companion object ALG-7d1fdc12, shard 2). Default unseeded runs keep os.urandom. Changeable here.

components.name: Python ssl sessions on default settings (OpenSSL version unknown)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Funding pipeline's live TLS: submits the signed QSB funding transaction and fetches fee data over HTTPS with Python ssl on default settings (host OpenSSL, unpinned — libssl-dev installed from distro apt). Default key exchange is classical ECDHE (X25519/P-256), no PQ groups offered; harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure is low-value here (public Bitcoin tx data, no credentials) but the sessions are quantum-unsafe. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The declared HTTPS client for the pipeline (Slipstream and mempool.space APIs); TLS posture = host OpenSSL defaults, version unpinned in requirements.txt.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The declared SSH client for driving rented vast.ai GPU hosts (pipeline/qsb_run.py, fleet and v16 orchestrator modules); paramiko version unpinned, so KEX/hostkey/cipher posture varies with the installed version; the call sites disable host-key verification (companion object ALG-ccf6c378, shard 2).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Unpinned requests dependency: ships TLS via the host OpenSSL; used by fund_qsb.py for funding-tx submission and fee APIs (see PROTO-dca6de59 for the sessions themselves).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Unpinned paramiko dependency: implements SSH-2 with its own crypto stack (curve25519/nistp ECDH KEX, ECDSA/RSA/Ed25519 host and user keys, AES-GCM/CTR + ChaCha20-Poly1305 depending on version); drives rented GPU hosts. Companion: host-key checking disabled at call sites (ALG-ccf6c378, shard 2).
